subject: MAP: Load test scheduling for Acme - traffic replay & capacity sizing
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Lee <john.lee@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Load test scheduling for Acme - traffic replay & capacity sizing

Thanks for the call earlier, John — good to align on scope. Per our discussion, I'm attaching a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that captures milestones, owners, and a proposed target close. The next milestone we agreed on is the load/performance test to validate dedicated capacity sizing with a traffic replay.

Quick recap of the load-test milestone:
- Objective: Validate dedicated capacity sizing for peak traffic and confirm latency & success-rate SLOs under production-like replay.
- Target window: 1 business day test window (preferably during low production hours).
- Peak QPS target: 1,200 peak, 300 steady-state (you mentioned ~1.1k peak; we bumped to 1.2k to include headroom).
- Key success criteria: 99th pct latency < 300ms, 99.5% success rate, acceptable token cost.
- Responsibilities: Acme to provide traffic snapshot + replay manifest; Redwood to provision dedicated capacity (GPU pool) and run traffic replay.
- Dependencies: traffic artifact, scoped test prompts, security checklist complete, and a runbook for rollback.

Proposed next steps:
1) Acme confirms traffic snapshot format and provides the manifest by Fri 3/13.
2) Redwood schedules the load test for the week of 3/22 — please confirm preferred dates/times.
3) Run test, capture metrics, and debrief within 48 hours.

I've attached the MAP draft and a short test-plan outline. Dev, can you add the rough capacity estimate (GPU type / count) once we get the manifest? Nikhil — I put you as the internal stakeholder for commercial sizing/commit.

John — any constraints from your side on the 3/22 week? If that doesn't work, propose alternative dates and we'll adapt.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

- 20260310-ACME-MAP-draft.xlsx
- acme-load-test-plan.pdf

Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Load test scheduling for Acme - traffic replay & capacity sizing

Thanks, Marissa — appreciate the summary. A few quick items from our side:

- The dates for week of 3/22 look good in principle. We'd prefer Tue 3/24 morning (PST) for the replay to align with our on-call. Can Redwood confirm availability?
- Traffic artifact: we'll provide a replay bundle (NDJSON events + manifest). What exact format/version do you need? I saw the manifest field in the MAP but want to avoid rework.
- Security: our security team needs a short list of required access (IP ranges, any temporary keys) before they sign off.

Also — curious how you calibrated the 1,200 peak QPS number. Our peak last month hit ~950 sustained for 15 minutes and burst to ~1,050; 1.2k is fine if it's headroom but please confirm cost delta if we size for 1.2k vs 1.05k.

I'll loop Samantha (platform eng) on the replay artifact.

—John

Hi John — quick technical notes on replay format, capacity, and what we'll need to run the test.

Replay artifact requirements (preferred):
- NDJSON with one event per line, fields: timestamp, user_id, prompt_id, prompt_text, response_length_hint, model_hint (optional).
- Manifest JSON listing sample rate, time range, and extracted 95th/99th token length distribution. We can accept gzipped tarball.
- Example: acme-traffic-replay-manifest.json (attached as sample manifest).

Capacity sizing (initial estimate):
- Based on the token distribution you mentioned and a 1,200 peak QPS target, we estimate a dedicated pool of 8 x A10G (or equivalent) GPUs for the 1 business-day run. That provides margin for transformers with 8k context and parallelism for batching.
- If you want to size to 1,050 peak only, we can run with 6 x A10G. Cost delta for the test day is roughly +25% for 8 GPUs vs 6 GPUs (estimate; we can provide an exact number once Nikhil confirms pricing).

Test window & orchestration:
- We prefer a 4–6 hour active test window within the selected day (ramp-up, steady-state, ramp-down). Full day reserved for validation & troubleshooting.
- We'll run the traffic replay from Redwood's test cluster against a dedicated model endpoint in your environment (Dedicated or Hosted with VPC peering — whichever you choose). For Private / on-prem we need the environment to be reachable via the agreed networking plan.

Prerequisites (to be completed before run):
1) Acme provides replay bundle + manifest at least 5 business days ahead (target 3/17).
2) Signed security checklist (listed items: IPs, user accounts, KMS access details if using encrypted artifacts).
3) Scoped prompt set for any dynamic prompts (to avoid PII leakage).

Deliverables after run: raw metrics (P50/P90/P95/P99 latencies), throughput graphs, error/success rates by prompt type, and a capacity recommendation write-up. We'll also produce a short cost estimate for running in production over a month with the chosen config.

Attachments: acme-traffic-replay-manifest.json (sample)

If Tue 3/24 AM works for you, we can reserve the pool and do a dry-run 24 hours earlier to validate the replay ingestion.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

- 3/23 09:00 PST: Redwood dry-run (ingest-only, no traffic)
- 3/24 08:00–12:00 PST: Live replay run (ramp + steady + ramp-down)
- 3/25: Results debrief and capacity recommendation

Target close for this MAP milestone: 2026-03-31 (to give time for procurement/commits).

Nikhil — can you confirm the commercial note (6 vs 8 GPU day delta) and provide the provisional test-day quote for Acme? Laura — can you own the post-run debrief scheduling and customer success readout?

John — if 3/24 AM works, reply with a quick sign-off so we can lock scheduling and start security sign-off. If not, propose an alternate 24–48 hour window that week.

Best,
Marissa
